tools.name: city_picks
tools.description: Instant and free: the latest finished standard search for one of the covered cities, about six weeks out, refreshed on a rota: whole homes for two adults and five nights in most cities, a six-adult weekend in New Orleans, Miami, Las Vegas, South Lake Tahoe, Sedona; stayType "hotel" gives the hotel-r

tools.name: get_activities
tools.description: Top-rated things to do on Viator for a search's spot and dates (what the trip is for first, the city's best otherwise), with a second place to look when the row is thin. Pass a searchId from search_stays or city_picks; intent overrides the search's own.

tools.name: set_alert
tools.description: Starts the otter's daily re-run of a finished search, emailing the key's account when a verified pick drops 5% or $50 or the cheapest pick disappears. Needs a key (stayotter.com/connect); the first alert is free with an account, more are Pro.

tools.description: Reads one place the traveler found themselves into the receipts a pick carries: where it is, whether the street is quiet or lively, bars, cafés and restaurants within a ten-minute walk, the distance to a spot they name and, with dates, the lowest total and the lowest they can still cancel, each read

tools.name: watch_booking
tools.description: For a stay already booked with free cancellation: pass the confirmation email's text. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "watch_booking" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: For a stay already booked with free cancellation: pass the confirmation email's text. The otter keeps five facts (property, dates, total paid, deadline, where i…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "watch_similar_homes" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: For a whole home already booked (watch_booking, then the first morning's read found the nights taken by the traveler): watches other verified whole homes nearby…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: watch_booking, watch_similar_homes · Private data: watch_booking · Public sink: watch_booking · Destructive: set_alert, watch_booking.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: watch_booking, watch_similar_homes · Private data: watch_booking · Public sink: watch_booking · Destructive: set_alert, watch_booking

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_stays" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
